claims.text: Current-dollar (nominal) PCE increased $23.7 billion (0.1 percent) in July 2022 from the preceding month. This is nominal spending at market prices, distinct from the PCE price index, which decreased 0.1 percent; real PCE increased 0.2 percent.

citations.quotation: personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $23.7 billion (0.1 percent). The PCE price index decreased 0.1 percent.
Current-dollar estimates are valued in the prices of the period when the transactions occurred—that is, at “market value.”

claims.text: The nominal increase reflected a $33.3 billion increase in spending for services, partly offset by a $9.6 billion decrease in spending for goods.

citations.quotation: $23.7 billion increase in current-dollar PCE in July reflected an increase of $33.3 billion in spending for services that was partly offset by a decrease of $9.6 billion in spending for goods

claims.text: The personal saving rate was 5.0 percent in July 2022, with personal saving of $932.3 billion.

citations.quotation: Personal saving was $932.3 billion in July and the personal saving rate—personal saving as a percentage of disposable personal income—was 5.0 percent

counterarguments.text: While nominal PCE rose 0.1 percent, the PCE price index fell 0.1 percent, showing the spending increase partly reflects price declines rather than volume; on an inflation-adjusted basis real PCE rose 0.2 percent. Also, goods spending fell in nominal terms ($9.6 billion) even as real goods spending rose 0.2 percent, since goods prices decreased 0.4 percent.

citations.quotation: Real DPI increased 0.3 percent in July and real PCE increased 0.2 percent; goods increased 0.2 percent and services increased 0.2 percent
Prices for goods decreased 0.4 percent and prices for services increased 0.1 percent.
